category_title: At-risk young adolescents exhibiting school refusal, performance anxiety, and rejection of teacher authority
minimal_context: The student is placing a cross on an emotion chart to reflect on their weekend and is being asked to explain their choice to the class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Good morning. Please take a red or green cross and place it on the emotion chart to show how you felt over the weekend.

STUDENT: (Places a red cross on the chart but stays silent, looking extremely shy.)

TUTOR: Now, can you justify your choice to the rest of the class and explain why you felt that way?

STUDENT: (Struggles to speak to the other kids in the class) I don't know.

TUTOR: Just try to verbalise your feelings. How might you change the circumstances if you were in that situation again?

STUDENT: I don't care. I'm never going to be more capable at this anyway.

options.A: Support the development of strong home and school partnerships through a communication journal sent home weekly with generic information about the emotion chart activities and personal comments about the student.
options.B: Adhere to a routine during the morning reflection, providing positive reinforcement for desired behaviors, such as social reinforcement or earning stickers during the emotion chart activity.
options.C: Ask follow-up questions during the emotion chart activity to model conversational skills for the student when they are speaking to the teacher and the rest of the class.
options.D: Provide training that involves modeling or providing examples and non-examples of the targeted behavior when the student is asked to justify their choice to the rest of the class.
